summary.title: Roll your own toy UNIX-clone OS
summary.one_liner: A practical tutorial series on writing a simple monolithic UNIX-like teaching kernel for x86 in C with some assembly.
takeaways: Build a simple UNIX-like monolithic kernel for x86 using C with some inline assembly
Understand that drivers are loaded as kernel-mode modules in this design, which is simpler than user-mode drivers
Know the prerequisites: GCC, ld, NASM and GNU Make, plus strong C pointer skills and basic Intel-syntax assembly
Find further help via the osdev.org wiki and forums, osdever.net, and alt.os.development
summary.summary: This is the introduction page of a multi-part tutorial that walks through building a simple UNIX-clone operating system for x86 in C, with assembly where needed. It explains that the kernel is monolithic, with drivers loaded as kernel-mode modules, and that it is a teaching kernel chosen for simplicity rather than efficiency. The page lists the required tools (GCC, ld, NASM, GNU Make) and background knowledge, and points to external resources such as the Intel manuals, osdev.org, and osdever.net. The rest of the series is a hands-on implementation guide, with theory given in each section.
